topic: Keeping the publications list on satishregonda.in current with minimal manual work: ORCID / Crossref / OpenAlex / Semantic Scholar / Google Scholar APIs benchmarked against Dr. Regonda's actual record, plus BibTeX/CSL rendering, legal PDF linking, a concrete build architecture, and Scholar-indexing metadata.
key_findings: IDENTIFIERS (verified live): Dr. Regonda is ORCID 0000-0003-3188-9415 and OpenAlex A5015401267. OpenAlex holds 55 works, 1,470 citations, h-index 13, i10 18. These are the two IDs the whole pipeline should key on.

COVERAGE IS WILDLY UNEQUAL — this is the single most decisive finding. For the SAME person: OpenAlex 55 works, ORCID public record 14 work-groups (25%), Crossref `filter=orcid:` only 5 works (9%). Crossref's ORCID filter only matches works where the publisher deposited the ORCID, and most did not. ORCID and Crossref-by-ORCID are both disqualified as the source of truth.

SEMANTIC SCHOLAR FRAGMENTS HIM across three author IDs — 98921407 (44 papers, 1338 citations, h12), 2340645204 (1 paper), 2331932788 (1 paper). Using S2 as the primary source silently loses papers unless you merge IDs by hand.

OPENALEX PRICING CHANGED IN FEB 2026 and most guides are stale. API keys are now expected. Measured anonymous headers: `x-ratelimit-limit: 1000`, `x-ratelimit-limit-usd: 0.1`, resetting at midnight UTC. A free key (openalex.org/settings/api, ~30 seconds) gives $1/day. Pass it as `?api_key=...` or an `Authorization: Bearer` header.

OPENALEX COST FOR THIS SITE IS EFFECTIVELY ZERO: fetching all 55 works in one call with `per-page=200` consumed exactly 1 credit / $0.0001 (`x-ratelimit-cost-usd: 0.0001`). A daily refresh uses 0.1% of even the anonymous allowance. `mailto=` no longer changes OpenAlex limits — it is vestigial there.
OPENALEX `per-page` MAX IS 200, NOT 100. Verified: per-page=200 returned 200 results; per-page=201 returned `Pagination error.` The help docs say 100 and are wrong.

CROSSREF POLITE POOL IS A MEASURED 3x: no mailto gives `x-rate-limit-limit: 1`, `x-concurrency-limit: 1`, `x-api-pool: public-array`; with mailto it gives `3`, `3`, `x-api-pool: polite-array`. Both the `?mailto=` query param AND `mailto:` inside the User-Agent header work identically.

ORCID PUBLIC API NEEDS NO TOKEN FOR READS. `https://pub.orcid.org/v3.0/{id}/works` returned HTTP 200 anonymously. Limits: anonymous 12 req/s, 40 burst, 25k reads/day per IP; registered public client 100k/day per Client ID; Member 24 req/s, no quota. The client-credentials token flow (`/oauth/token`, `grant_type=client_credentials`, `scope=/read-public`, ~20-year token) exists but is unnecessary here.

CITATION COUNTS DIVERGE BY UP TO 38% ACROSS SOURCES. For his flagship paper 10.1175/jcli-3272.1: OpenAlex 524, Semantic Scholar 514, Crossref 380. For 10.3390/w13091224: OpenAlex 11, Crossref 11, S2 9. Google Scholar would report a fourth, higher number. Any citation count on the site must be labelled with its source and date, or omitted.

GOOGLE SCHOLAR'S robots.txt SETTLES THE SCRAPING QUESTION. It contains `Allow: /citations?user=` but also `Disallow: /citations?*cstart=`. The profile's first page is crawlable; the pagination parameter every scraper needs to read a full profile is explicitly disallowed. There is no official API. `scholarly` requires rotating proxies/CAPTCHA solving. SerpApi is the only clean paid route: free 250 searches/mo, Starter $25/mo for 1,000, Developer $75/mo for 5,000.

OPENALEX'S 55 WORKS CONTAIN HEAVY NOISE that would embarrass him if published raw: 9 conference-abstracts (mostly 'AGU Fall Meeting Abstracts'), 2 dissertations (his own 2006 PhD thesis and a student's), 5 preprints, 16 works with no DOI, and one entry whose title is a parsing artifact scraped from a reference list: '2004), Temporal scaling in river flow: Can it be chaotic'. Filtering to type in {article, book-chapter, conference-paper} cuts 55 to 39.

NAIVE TITLE DEDUP DESTROYS REAL PAPERS. Clustering his works on a 60-char normalized title prefix produced 4 clusters, one of which is a FALSE POSITIVE: 10.1016/j.jhydrol.2014.05.028 ('...HEFS: 1. Experimental design and forcing verification', 52 cites) and 10.1016/j.jhydrol.2014.05.030 ('...HEFS: 2. Streamflow verification', 51 cites) are two legitimate papers in a two-part series. Dedup on DOI first, full normalized title only as fallback — never a prefix.

GENUINE DUPLICATES SPLIT HIS CITATIONS. Two real duplicate pairs exist where a DOI-bearing record and a DOI-less stub coexist: npg-12-397-2005 (55 cites) vs a 0-DOI twin (2 cites), and j.jhydrol.2013.05.028 (60 cites) vs a 0-DOI 2010 twin (0 cites). Keep the DOI-bearing record.

HIS OWN NAME IS PERFECTLY CLEAN BUT HIS COAUTHORS' ARE NOT. Because his ORCID is attached, OpenAlex renders him identically ('Satish Kumar Regonda', A5015401267) across all 55 works — so the self-highlight rule is trivially deterministic. But coauthors fragment badly: Balaji Rajagopalan has 3 OpenAlex IDs, Kambhammettu 2 ('B. V. N. P. Kambhammettu' / 'BVN P Kambhammettu'), Azharuddin 2 ('Azharuddin Mohammed' / 'M. Azharuddin'), and one authorship has a null author id. 17 of 77 distinct coauthor names begin with initials. A student-asterisk rule keyed on either name OR OpenAlex ID alone will miss entries.

`filter=author.orcid:https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3188-9415` returns the SAME 55 works as `filter=author.id:A5015401267`. Key the query on ORCID — it is permanent and he controls it — rather than on the OpenAlex author ID, which can merge or split.

LEGAL PDF PICTURE: only 18 of 55 works are OA, and only 10 of 55 expose a direct `best_oa_location.pdf_url`. Licences break down as 9 cc-by, 3 cc-by-nc, 1 cc-by-nc-nd, 1 other-oa, and 4 with NO licence at all (oa_status 'bronze' — free to read on the publisher site, but not re-hostable). Only the cc-by set is safe to mirror as a local PDF.

DOI CONTENT NEGOTIATION WORKS AND NEEDS NO API: `curl -LH 'Accept: application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json' https://doi.org/10.3390/w13091224` returns CSL-JSON; `Accept: application/x-bibtex` returns BibTeX; `Accept: text/x-bibliography; style=apa` returns a fully formatted citation string server-side.

DOI RESOLUTION IS CASE-INSENSITIVE (verified: both 10.1175/JCLI-3272.1 and 10.1175/jcli-3272.1 return HTTP 302 to the identical target). OpenAlex lowercases all DOIs; Semantic Scholar uppercases them ('10.3390/W13091224'). Lowercase DOIs for dedup keys; the cosmetic case difference does not break links.

RENDERING STACK VERIFIED WORKING: citation-js 0.8.2 ships only apa, vancouver and harvard1 built in; any other CSL style must be registered via `plugins.config.get('@csl').styles.add('agu', cslText)` (the method is `styles.add`, NOT `templates.add` as older docs show). american-geophysical-union.csl and american-meteorological-society.csl exist in the CSL repo; water-resources-research.csl does NOT (404). bibtexparser's stable release is still 1.4.4 — v2 remains beta at 2.0.0b10.

HIS CURRENT PAGE HAS SIX SECTIONS AND THE APIs COVER ONLY TWO. sites.google.com/.../products-publications is organised as A. Products (web tools), B. In Referred Journals, C. Book Chapters, D. Presentations at Conferences, E. Invited Seminars, F. Scientific activities. No API carries A, D, E or F. Any design that assumes 'the publications page is generated from an API' will silently drop two-thirds of his page structure.

GITHUB ACTIONS CRON WILL SILENTLY DIE ON THIS REPO. Scheduled workflows in public repos are auto-disabled after 60 days with no commit activity, and cron runs can be delayed 15+ minutes or skipped entirely with no error. A publications-refresh job that only commits when something changes will stop committing during a quiet spell and then be disabled — exactly the failure mode this site is prone to.

al-folio ALREADY SOLVES THE ASTERISK AND FEATURED PROBLEMS and its conventions are worth copying verbatim: `selected={true}` is the featured flag; custom bib fields include abbr, bibtex_show, pdf, code, website, award, altmetric, dimensions, preview, annotation; and self-highlighting strips marker glyphs before matching with `author.last | regex_replace: '[*∗†‡§¶‖&^]', ''` — meaning asterisks are stored INSIDE the BibTeX author name (`author={Einstein*†, A. and ...}`) with a legend in `annotation={...}`.

GOOGLE SCHOLAR INDEXING RULES (from the official inclusion page): supply at minimum (1) citation_title, (2) the full name of at least the first author, (3) year. Missing any one causes the page to be 'processed as if they had no meta tags at all'. Dates use the `2010/5/12` format. Each author needs its OWN separate `citation_author` tag with no affiliations or degrees. PDFs are only indexed if linked from the HTML page via `citation_pdf_url`. Verified live on arxiv.org/abs/2411.05233, which emits exactly this pattern (though it uses `citation_date` rather than `citation_publication_date`).

END-TO-END PIPELINE BUILT AND PROVEN: I wrote and ran a build script that pulls OpenAlex by ORCID, filters types, dedupes DOI-first, applies a Google-Sheet-shaped override layer (featured / student / venue-fix / exclude / manual), and emits publications.json. It reduced 55 raw works to 38 clean entries and produced byte-identical output across repeated runs.
recommendations: MAKE A COMMITTED FILE THE CANONICAL SOURCE, NOT AN API. `content/publications.json` (or .bib) in the repo is what the site renders. OpenAlex is a *proposer*, never the authority. This is the only way to satisfy 'the site must not change under him' — the site changes when a file changes, and file changes are reviewable.

QUERY OPENALEX BY ORCID, NOT BY AUTHOR ID OR NAME: `https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=author.orcid:https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3188-9415&per-page=200&select=...&sort=publication_date:desc`. Verified to return all 55 works in one call for 1 credit. Get a free API key and store it as a repo secret; do not rely on the anonymous 1000-credit tier for a production job.

HAVE THE SCHEDULED JOB OPEN A PULL REQUEST, NOT PUSH TO MAIN. Run weekly (`cron: '0 3 * * 1'`), diff the fetched set against the committed file, and if there are new entries open a PR titled e.g. '3 new publications found'. Nothing reaches the live site without a human merge. This makes the pipeline deterministic and gives him a natural review moment.

ADD `workflow_dispatch` AND A KEEPALIVE. Because public-repo scheduled workflows die after 60 days of inactivity, add a manual `workflow_dispatch` trigger and have the job touch a `data/last-checked.txt` timestamp and commit it even when no publications changed. That single commit keeps the schedule alive and gives you a visible heartbeat.

FILTER AGGRESSIVELY BY TYPE, THEN LET HIM VETO. Keep only `article`, `book-chapter`, `conference-paper` (55 → 39). This removes all 9 AGU/EGU abstracts, both dissertations and the reference-list parsing artifact. Put an `exclude` column in the override sheet so he can kill anything else with one row.

DEDUPE DOI-FIRST, FULL-TITLE-SECOND, NEVER BY PREFIX. Use lowercased DOI as the primary key; for DOI-less records fall back to the FULL normalized title. Prefer the record that has a DOI, then the higher citation count. Prefix matching would have merged his two-part HEFS papers (j.jhydrol.2014.05.028 and .030) into one.

BUILD THE OVERRIDE LAYER AS A GOOGLE SHEET PUBLISHED AS CSV — this is the lever that satisfies the 'professor edits it himself' constraint. `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<ID>/gviz/tq?tqx=out:csv&sheet=Publications` is verified working and needs no API key or OAuth. Suggested columns: doi | featured | student_authors | venue_override | title_override | pdf_url | exclude | notes. The build fetches this CSV, merges it over the OpenAlex data, and commits the result.

GIVE HIM A SECOND SHEET FOR THE FOUR SECTIONS NO API COVERS. His page has Products, Conference Presentations, Invited Seminars and Scientific Activities — none of which exist in OpenAlex, Crossref, ORCID or S2. A `Manual` sheet with columns section | year | citation_text | url is the entire solution, and it is the part he will use most.

KEY THE SELF-HIGHLIGHT ON ORCID, THE STUDENT-ASTERISK ON A MANUAL ALIAS LIST. His own ORCID appears on every one of the 55 authorships, so `authorship.author.orcid === 'https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3188-9415'` is a 100%-reliable bold rule. Students cannot be matched that way (Rajagopalan alone has 3 OpenAlex IDs), so maintain a `students` sheet mapping every observed name spelling to one student, and mark on that alias set.

RENDER AT BUILD TIME, SHIP STATIC HTML. Use citation-js 0.8.2 + american-geophysical-union.csl (registered via `styles.add`), which matches the AGU/AMS conventions of his field, and precompute the formatted string into publications.json. Do not run citeproc in the browser — it is a large dependency for output that never changes between deploys.

APPLY THE BOLD/ASTERISK MARKUP AFTER CSL FORMATTING, NOT BEFORE. CSL will re-order and abbreviate names, so inject `` by regex on the rendered string (verified working: `Regonda, S. K.` → `Regonda, S. K.`). Alternatively adopt al-folio's trick of embedding the marker in the name and stripping `[*∗†‡§¶‖&^]` before comparison.

EITHER OMIT CITATION COUNTS OR LABEL THEM HONESTLY. Given the 524/514/380 spread on his most-cited paper, a bare number invites 'that's wrong, Scholar says more'. Best: show no per-paper counts, and instead link out to his Google Scholar profile for metrics. If he insists, render 'Cited by 524 (OpenAlex, Sep 2026)' with the source and date baked in.

LINK PDFs, HOST ONLY THE cc-by ONES. Use `best_oa_location.pdf_url` when present (10 of 55) and fall back to the DOI link. Only mirror a PDF locally when `best_oa_location.license` starts with `cc-by` (9 works qualify). Never host the 4 'bronze' works — they have no licence at all, only free-to-read status on the publisher's site.

EMIT HIGHWIRE META TAGS ON EVERY PER-PAPER PAGE if you give papers their own URLs: citation_title, one citation_author per author, citation_publication_date in `2026/7/2` form, citation_journal_title, citation_volume, citation_firstpage/citation_lastpage, citation_doi, and citation_pdf_url pointing at any PDF you host. Without citation_pdf_url, Scholar will not index a hosted PDF at all.

ADD schema.org JSON-LD: a single `Person` node for him (name, jobTitle, affiliation → Organization 'Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad', sameAs → his ORCID, Google Scholar and OpenAlex URLs) reused by @id across pages, plus `ScholarlyArticle` nodes on paper pages using headline, author, datePublished, isPartOf → Periodical, pageStart/pageEnd, and identifier as a PropertyValue with propertyID 'DOI'.

USE THE CROSSREF POLITE POOL ONLY AS AN ENRICHMENT PASS. It is not a discovery source for him (5 works), but it is the best source for exact volume/issue/page and publisher-canonical journal titles. Set `User-Agent: satishregonda.in (https://satishregonda.in; mailto:...)` to get 3 req/s, and only call it for DOIs that OpenAlex already gave you.

MAINTAIN A SMALL JOURNAL-NAME OVERRIDE MAP IN CODE. OpenAlex ships real defects in his venue names: 'npj natural hazards.' (lowercase, trailing period), 'Journal of Hydrology Regional Studies' (missing colon), 'Nonlinear processes in geophysics' (lowercase), 'EGUGA'. Four or five hardcoded fixes plus a sheet column covers it.

SKIP SEMANTIC SCHOLAR AND SERPAPI FOR V1. S2 adds influentialCitationCount and tldr, but tldr was null for his paper and he is split across 3 author IDs; SerpApi costs $25+/mo to restate numbers he can already link to. Neither earns its complexity on a site whose main problem is curation, not data volume.

TREAT BIBTEX-FROM-SCHOLAR AS THE FALLBACK, NOT THE PLAN. It is a real option — he selects all on his profile and exports .bib — but it is a manual step he must remember, Scholar's BibTeX omits DOIs and mangles venue names, and its author strings vary ('S. Regonda' vs 'Satish K. Regonda') which breaks the self-highlight rule that OpenAlex gives you for free. Keep the parser in the codebase so a hand-curated .bib can always override the API, but do not make it the primary loop.
details:
## 0. Verified identifiers for Dr. Regonda | Thing | Value | |---|---| | ORCID | `0000-0003-3188-9415` | | OpenAlex author | `A5015401267` | | Semantic Scholar | `98921407` (primary, 44 papers) + `2340645204` + `2331932788` | | OpenAlex works / citations | 55 works, 1,470 citations, h-index 13, i10 18 | Everything below was measured against his real record on 2026-09-04. --- ## 1. Coverage benchmark — the decisive table Same person, same day, four sources: | Source | Query | Works returned | |---|---|---| | **OpenAlex** | `filter=author.id:A5015401267` | **55** | | **OpenAlex** | `filter=author.orcid:https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3188-9415` | **55** | | ORCID public | `pub.orcid.org/v3.0/0000-0003-3188-9415/works` | **14** groups | | Crossref | `filter=orcid:0000-0003-3188-9415` | **5** | | Semantic Scholar | author `98921407` | 44 (+2 stranded on other IDs) | Crossref's ORCID filter only matches works where the *publisher* deposited the ORCID into the DOI record. Most of his publishers did not. This is why Crossref-by-ORCID returns 9% of his output. Crossref by **author name** is worse than useless — `query.author=Regonda` returns 100 results dominated by an unrelated "Dr. Regonda Nagaraju" publishing on NLP and speech emotion detection. Never query by surname. --- ## 2. OpenAlex ### 2.1 Pricing changed in February 2026 (most guides are stale) Measured response headers, **anonymous**: ``` x-ratelimit-limit: 1000 x-ratelimit-limit-usd: 0.1 x-ratelimit-remaining: 987 x-ratelimit-cost-usd: 0.0001 x-ratelimit-credits-used: 1 x-ratelimit-reset: 45432 # seconds to midnight UTC ``` - **Anonymous**: 1,000 credits/day, **$0.10/day**. Documented as "a few calls… for demo purposes, not suitable for any kind of production use." - **Free API key**: **$1/day** (10× anonymous). Sign up at openalex.org, key at `openalex.org/settings/api`. Docs quote the $1/day as covering ~10,000 list/filter calls, 1,000 searches, or 100 content downloads. - Passed as `?api_key=YOUR_KEY` **or** an `Authorization: Bearer` header. - Per-operation: single entity lookup $0, list/filter **$0.0001**, search **$0.001**, PDF/XML download **$0.01**. - Paid tiers: pay-as-you-go in $1 increments (expire after 3 months); Member $5,000/yr ($20/day); Member+ $10,000/yr ($100/day); Partner from $20,000/yr. - `/rate-limit` endpoint requires a key: anonymous returns `{"error": "Authentication required"}`. - **`mailto=` no longer affects OpenAlex limits.** With and without it, headers were identical. The polite-pool convention survives at Crossref and Unpaywall, not here. ### 2.2 The whole job costs one credit ```bash curl "https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=author.orcid:https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3188-9415\ &per-page=200\ &select=id,doi,title,publication_year,publication_date,type,cited_by_count,best_oa_location,open_access,primary_location,biblio,authorships\ &sort=publication_date:desc&api_key=$OPENALEX_KEY" ``` → all 55 works, `"cost_usd": 0.0001`, `x-ratelimit-credits-used: 1`. **`per-page` max is 200**, not the documented 100 (verified: 200 → 200 results; 201 → `Pagination error.`). Cursor paging via `&cursor=*` → `meta.next_cursor` works if you ever need it. ### 2.3 Work record shape (trimmed) ```json { "id": "https://openalex.org/W7167055507", "doi": "https://doi.org/10.1038/s44304-026-00234-3", "title": "Web-messaging-based dissemination of urban rainfall and flood information: a Telegram bot framework", "publication_year": 2026, "publication_date": "2026-07-02", "type": "article", "cited_by_count": 0, "open_access": { "is_oa": true, "oa_status": "gold", "oa_url": "...", "any_repository_has_fulltext": false }, "best_oa_location": { "is_oa": true, "landing_page_url": "https://doi.org/...", "pdf_url": "https://journals.ametsoc.org/downloadpdf/journals/clim/18/2/jcli-3272.1.pdf", "license": "cc-by", "version": "publishedVersion", "source": { "display_name": "npj natural hazards.", "issn_l": "2948-2100", "is_in_doaj": true } }, "biblio": { "volume": null, "issue": null, "first_page": null, "last_page": null }, "primary_topic": { "display_name": "Flood Risk Assessment and Management", "field": { "display_name": "Environmental Science" } }, "authorships": [ { "author_position": "last", "author": { "id": "https://openalex.org/A5015401267", "display_name": "Satish Kumar Regonda", "orcid": "https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3188-9415" }, "raw_author_name": "Satish Kumar Regonda" } ] } ``` `primary_topic` / `topics` give you free, credible subject tags ("Flood Risk Assessment and Management", "Water Science and Technology") if you want filter chips on the publications page without hand-tagging. ### 2.4 What's actually wrong with his 55 records ``` types: article 34 | conference-abstract 9 | preprint 5 | conference-paper 3 | book-chapter 2 | dissertation 2 has DOI: 39/55 is_oa: 18/55 best_oa_location.pdf_url: 10/55 oa_status: closed 37 | gold 13 | bronze 3 | green 2 ``` Noise you must strip: - 9 × `conference-abstract`, mostly `AGU Fall Meeting Abstracts` / `EGU General Assembly Conference Abstracts` - 2 × `dissertation` — his own 2006 CU Boulder thesis *and* a student's 2019 IITH thesis - 1 garbage record: title `"2004), Temporal scaling in river flow: Can it be chaotic"` — scraped out of a reference list - venue name defects: `'npj natural hazards.'`, `'EGUGA'`, `'Journal of Hydrology Regional Studies'` (missing colon), `'Nonlinear processes in geophysics'`, `'HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)'` Filtering to `type ∈ {article, book-chapter, conference-paper}` → 39 works. ### 2.5 Duplicates — and the trap Clustering on a 60-char normalized title prefix found 4 clusters. **Two are genuine, one is a false positive that would delete a real paper:** | Cluster | Verdict | |---|---| | `10.1016/j.jhydrol.2013.05.028` (60 cites) vs DOI-less 2010 twin (0 cites) | genuine duplicate | | `10.5194/npg-12-397-2005` (55 cites) vs DOI-less twin (2 cites) | genuine duplicate — **citations are split across both** | | 2020 conference-abstract vs 2024 preprint, "Identification of flood events using Sentinel 2…" | genuine (type filter removes both) | | `10.1016/j.jhydrol.2014.05.028` vs `.030` | ❌ **FALSE POSITIVE** | The false positive in full: - `.028` → "Verification of temperature, precipitation, and streamflow forecasts from the NOAA/NWS Hydrologic Ensemble Forecast Service (HEFS): **1. Experimental design and forcing verification**" (52 cites) - `.030` → "…(HEFS): **2. Streamflow verification**" (51 cites) Two-part papers share long prefixes. **Dedup on DOI; use the full normalized title only as a fallback.** ### 2.6 Author-name reality (matters a lot for an Indian research group) His own name is immaculate — **one** OpenAlex ID, **one** spelling, across all 55 works, because his ORCID is attached. So the bold-my-name rule is a one-line ORCID comparison. His coauthors are not: ``` distinct coauthor names: 77 names starting with initials: 17 (e.g. 'B. V. N. P. Kambhammettu', 'M.P. Clark', 'P. P. Mujumdar') null author ids: 1 same person, multiple OpenAlex IDs: Balaji Rajagopalan -> A5089004731, A5102008092, A5146810894 'B. V. N. P. Kambhammettu' -> A5027162932 | 'BVN P Kambhammettu' -> A5110805369 'Azharuddin Mohammed' -> A5016926343 | 'M. Azharuddin' -> A5052717595 ``` Consequence: a student-asterisk rule keyed on name **or** on OpenAlex author ID will miss entries. It needs a manual alias set per student. Also: naive `given/family` splitting on `display_name` is unsafe here — `"S.R. Saipriya"` has no comma and no reliable order. --- ## 3. Crossref REST API ### 3.1 Polite pool, measured ``` no mailto: x-rate-limit-limit: 1 x-concurrency-limit: 1 x-api-pool: public-array ?mailto=you@example.com x-rate-limit-limit: 3 x-concurrency-limit: 3 x-api-pool: polite-array User-Agent: "... (mailto:you@example.com)" → identical polite-array result ``` Both mechanisms work; the User-Agent form is preferable because it also identifies the site. Recommended header: ``` User-Agent: satishregonda.in/1.0 (https://satishregonda.in; mailto:regonda@ce.iith.ac.in) ``` Note `x-rate-limit-*` headers are returned even on a `HEAD` (which itself 405s — use GET). Back off on HTTP 429. Crossref explicitly steers bulk users to their annual public data file rather than the API. ### 3.2 Useful shapes `?select=` trims the payload: ``` https://api.crossref.org/works/10.3390/w13091224 https://api.crossref.org/works?filter=orcid:0000-0003-3188-9415&rows=1000&select=DOI,title,author,container-title,issued,volume,page,link,license,is-referenced-by-count ``` Returns `author[].{given,family,ORCID,authenticated-orcid,affiliation[].name}`, `container-title[]`, `issued.date-parts`, `license[].{URL,content-version}`, `link[].URL`, `is-referenced-by-count`, and a JATS-wrapped `abstract`. `authenticated-orcid: true` is a genuinely useful signal — it means the ORCID was verified at submission, not just typed in. Crossref stores AMS DOIs lowercase (`10.1175/jcli-3272.1`), so its `DOI` field is not a reliable source of "canonical case" either. --- ## 4. ORCID Public API - **No token needed for reads.** `curl -H "Accept: application/json" https://pub.orcid.org/v3.0/0000-0003-3188-9415/works` → HTTP 200. - Token flow if you want one: POST `https://orcid.org/oauth/token` with `client_id`, `client_secret`, `grant_type=client_credentials`, `scope=/read-public`. Token lasts ~20 years. - **Rate limits**: anonymous 12 req/s, 40 burst, **25k reads/day per IP**; registered public client 12 req/s, **100k reads/day per Client ID**; Member 24 req/s, no quota. Burst overflow → HTTP 503. Endpoints: ``` /v3.0/{orcid}/works → summaries, grouped by external-id /v3.0/{orcid}/works/{pc1},{pc2},... → bulk detail, max 100 put-codes /v3.0/{orcid}/record → everything /v3.0/expanded-search/?q=family-name:Regonda ``` `/works` returns `group[]`, each with `work-summary[]` carrying `put-code`, `title.title.value`, `journal-title.value`, `type`, `publication-date.{year,month,day}`, `url.value`, `external-ids`, and a `source` block naming who asserted it (e.g. `"Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute"`). **Two disqualifying problems:** 1. Only 14 groups vs OpenAlex's 55 — it is only as complete as he keeps it. 2. **Privacy hazard**: the bulk `contributors` block leaks coauthor email addresses in cleartext (I saw a real `contributor-email` in his record). Never pipe raw ORCID JSON to the site. ORCID is worth using for exactly one thing: as the *stable identifier* that keys the OpenAlex query. --- ## 5. Semantic Scholar Graph API - Base: `https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1` - **Unauthenticated**: ~1,000 req/s *shared across all anonymous users*, throttled harder under load — in practice unpredictable. - **With a key**: 1 req/s dedicated. Request at `semanticscholar.org/product/api`, delivered by email, sent as `x-api-key`. Counterintuitively the key gives a *lower* nominal ceiling but a reliable one. ``` /author/search?query=Satish+Regonda&fields=name,paperCount,citationCount,hIndex,externalIds /author/{id}/papers?fields=title,year,venue,externalIds,citationCount,influentialCitationCount,openAccessPdf,publicationTypes,authors&limit=100 /paper/DOI:10.3390/w13091224?fields=title,tldr,influentialCitationCount,openAccessPdf,fieldsOfStudy /paper/batch (POST, up to 500 ids) ``` Gotchas found live: - **`tldr` is rejected on `/author/{id}/papers`** → `400 {"error":"Unrecognized or unsupported fields: [tldr]"}`. It only exists on `/paper/*` endpoints. - **`tldr` was `null`** for his 2021 Water paper — coverage is patchy, so you cannot promise auto-summaries. - **`openAccessPdf` can be `{"url": "", "status": null, "license": null}`** — an empty string, not null. Truthiness checks on `.url` are required. - S2 **uppercases DOIs** (`10.3390/W13091224`, `10.1175/JCLI-3272.1`). - `openAccessPdf` carries a `disclaimer` string pointing back at Unpaywall. What it genuinely adds: `influentialCitationCount` (39 for his JCLI paper vs 514 total) — a nicer "impact" signal than a raw count if you want one. --- ## 6. Google Scholar **There is no official API.** Three routes evaluated: ### 6.1 Scraping — settled by robots.txt `https://scholar.google.com/robots.txt` contains: ``` Disallow: /scholar Disallow: /citations? Allow: /citations?user= Disallow: /citations?*cstart= Allow: /citations?view_op=list_classic_articles ``` The profile's **first page is explicitly allowed**, but `cstart=` — the pagination parameter any tool needs to read a full profile — is **explicitly disallowed**. Reading his complete publication list by machine cannot be done within robots.txt. `scholar.google.com/citations?user=…` returned HTTP 302 to me even with a browser UA. ### 6.2 `scholarly` (Python) Works for small reads, but `search_pubs` / `citedby` trigger blocking and eventual IP bans; the package's own docs tell you to configure rotating proxies. Unsuitable for an unattended GitHub Action. ### 6.3 SerpApi Verified pricing: **Free 250 searches/mo**, Starter **$25/mo → 1,000**, Developer **$75/mo → 5,000**, Production **$150/mo → 15,000** (adds US Legal Shield), Big Data **$275/mo → 30,000**. A monthly profile refresh would sit inside the free tier — but it buys numbers he can simply *link to*. ### 6.4 Manual BibTeX export — the honest verdict Procedure: Scholar → My Profile → select-all checkbox → Export → BibTeX → `.bib` downloads. **It is not the pragmatic winner here, and it is close.** Arguments against: - It is a manual step he must remember — the exact failure mode this brief exists to eliminate. - Scholar's BibTeX omits DOIs, mangles venue names, and gives inconsistent author strings (`S. Regonda` vs `Satish K. Regonda`), which breaks the self-highlight rule OpenAlex hands you for free. - The select-all checkbox only selects *rendered* rows, so he must "Show more" to the end first — easy to get wrong and silently truncate. Arguments for: it is the only source that matches the numbers he quotes in talks, it needs no keys, and it captures items OpenAlex misses. **Recommendation: keep a BibTeX importer in the codebase as an override path, but drive the loop from OpenAlex.** A hand-curated `.bib` should always be able to win. --- ## 7. BibTeX / CSL rendering — tested, with the API corrections Current versions checked on the registries: | Package | Version | Note | |---|---|---| | `@citation-js/core`, `-plugin-bibtex`, `-plugin-csl` | **0.8.2** | | | `citeproc` | 2.4.63 | the CSL engine underneath | | `bibtexparser` (PyPI) | **1.4.4 stable** | v2 still beta at `2.0.0b10` — do not ship v2 | | `pybtex` | 0.26.1 | | | `citeproc-py` | 0.11.1 | | | `pyalex` | 0.21 | | | `habanero` | 2.9.2 | Crossref client | CSL styles (raw.githubusercontent.com/citation-style-language/styles/master/): - `american-geophysical-union.csl` ✅ 200 (24,412 bytes) - `american-meteorological-society.csl` ✅ 200 - `apa.csl` ✅ 200 - `water-resources-research.csl` ❌ **404 — does not exist** ### 7.1 Corrected citation-js API Older docs show `config.templates.add(...)`. In **0.8.2 that throws**. The real API: ```js const cfg = plugins.config.get('@csl') cfg.styles.add('agu', fs.readFileSync('agu.csl', 'utf8')) // cfg.styles.list() => ['apa','vancouver','harvard1'] ← only these ship built in ``` ### 7.2 Verified working render ```js import { Cite, plugins } from '@citation-js/core' import '@citation-js/plugin-bibtex' import '@citation-js/plugin-csl' const cfg = plugins.config.get('@csl') cfg.styles.add('agu', fs.readFileSync('agu.csl', 'utf8')) let html = new Cite(cslJson).format('bibliography', { format: 'html', template: 'agu' }) html = html.replace(/Regonda,\s*S\.\s*K\.?/g, 'Regonda, S. K.') ``` Real output: > • Ponukumati, P., & **Regonda, S. K.** (2026). Web-messaging-based dissemination of urban rainfall and flood information: a Telegram bot framework. *Npj Natural Hazards.* https://doi.org/10.1038/s44304-026-00234-3 Note `&` — citation-js emits a numeric entity for the ampersand. Harmless in HTML, breaks if you treat the string as plain text. ### 7.3 OpenAlex → CSL-JSON mapping ```js { id, type: 'article-journal', // 'book-chapter' -> 'chapter' title: w.title, 'container-title': w.primary_location.source.display_name, volume: w.biblio.volume, issue: w.biblio.issue, page: `${first_page}-${last_page}`, DOI: w.doi.replace('https://doi.org/', ''), issued: { 'date-parts': [[2026, 7, 2]] }, author: [{ family, given }] } ``` ### 7.4 Zero-dependency alternative: DOI content negotiation ```bash curl -LH "Accept: application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json" https://doi.org/10.3390/w13091224 curl -LH "Accept: application/x-bibtex" https://doi.org/10.3390/w13091224 curl -LH "Accept: text/x-bibliography; style=apa" https://doi.org/10.3390/w13091224 ``` The third returns a finished citation server-side: > Sharma, V. C., & Regonda, S. K. (2021). Multi-Spatial Resolution Rainfall-Runoff Modelling—A Case Study of Sabari River Basin, India. *Water*, 13(9), 1224. https://doi.org/10.3390/w13091224 Good for a one-off backfill; one request per DOI makes it wrong for the main loop. --- ## 8. PDFs, DOIs, arXiv, Unpaywall ### DOI case Verified case-insensitive — both `10.1175/JCLI-3272.1` and `10.1175/jcli-3272.1` return `HTTP 302 → http://journals.ametsoc.org/doi/10.1175/JCLI-3272.1`. **Lowercase DOIs as dedup keys.** (Publisher sites may 403 a bare curl; that is bot-blocking, not a DOI problem.) ### Unpaywall `https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/{doi}?email=YOUR@EMAIL` — **rejects placeholder addresses**: ```json {"HTTP_status_code":422,"error":true, "message":"Please use your own email address in API calls."} ``` A real address is mandatory. **You almost certainly don't need it**: OpenAlex already ingests Unpaywall and exposes the same data as `best_oa_location` and `open_access.oa_status`. ### arXiv `https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:hydroclimatology&start=0&max_results=1` — Atom XML, verified working. **HTTPS only** (plain `http://export.arxiv.org` returned empty). Only relevant if he starts preprinting; his current preprints are on Research Square and ESSOAr, not arXiv. ### What he may legally host All 18 OA works, with licence and version: ``` 2026 gold cc-by-nc publishedVersion pdf_url ✓ 2026 gold cc-by acceptedVersion 2026 gold (none) publishedVersion 2025 gold cc-by-nc-nd publishedVersion pdf_url ✓ 2025 gold cc-by-nc publishedVersion 2023 green cc-by acceptedVersion pdf_url ✓ 2021 gold cc-by publishedVersion pdf_url ✓ (×3) 2021 gold cc-by acceptedVersion (×2) 2020 gold cc-by-nc acceptedVersion 2020 gold cc-by acceptedVersion 2016 bronze (none) publishedVersion pdf_url ✓ 2005 bronze (none) publishedVersion pdf_url ✓ 2005 gold cc-by publishedVersion pdf_url ✓ 2005 green other-oa submittedVersion 2004 bronze (none) publishedVersion pdf_url ✓ licences: cc-by 9 | cc-by-nc 3 | cc-by-nc-nd 1 | other-oa 1 | none 4 versions: publishedVersion 11 | acceptedVersion 6 | submittedVersion 1 ``` **Rules:** - `license` starts with `cc-by` → safe to mirror locally with attribution (9 works). - `oa_status: bronze` with `license: null` (4 works) → free to *read* on the publisher's site, **no licence granted**. Link only, never host. - 37 works are closed → DOI link only. - Author *accepted* manuscripts (6 works) are usually postable under publisher self-archiving policies after an embargo — check SHERPA RoMEO per journal; don't automate this. --- ## 9. Recommended architecture ``` ┌──────────────────────────────┐ │ OpenAlex filter=author.orcid │ proposer, never authority └──────────────┬───────────────┘ │ weekly GitHub Action ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ fetch → filter types → dedupe (DOI first) │ │ → merge Google Sheet overrides → normalize │ └──────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘ │ diff vs committed file ▼ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │ opens a PULL REQUEST │ ← human merges; site never self-mutates └──────────────┬──────────────┘ ▼ content/publications.json ← CANONICAL, in git │ ▼ build: citation-js + AGU CSL → static HTML ``` ### 9.1 Why a committed file is canonical It is the only design that satisfies "the site must not change under him." The site renders a file; the file changes only via a reviewed commit. A live API call at page load or at every deploy means an upstream metadata edit silently rewrites his CV. ### 9.2 The Action ```yaml name: Refresh publications on: schedule: [{ cron: '0 3 * * 1' }] # Mondays 03:00 UTC workflow_dispatch: # manual trigger — also the 60-day keepalive permissions: { contents: write, pull-requests: write } jobs: refresh: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: { node-version: '22' } - run: npm ci - run: node scripts/build-publications.mjs env: OPENALEX_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENALEX_KEY }} OVERRIDES_CSV_URL: ${{ secrets.OVERRIDES_CSV_URL }} - uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6 with: branch: pubs/auto-refresh title: 'Publications refresh' commit-message: 'chore: refresh publications from OpenAlex' ``` **Two GitHub Actions traps that will bite this specific repo:** 1. Public-repo scheduled workflows are **auto-disabled after 60 days with no repository activity**. A job that only commits when publications change will go quiet, then be disabled. Fix: always write `data/last-checked.txt` with a UTC timestamp and commit it, so every run is activity. 2. Cron is best-effort — runs are routinely delayed 15+ minutes and can be **skipped entirely with no error or notification**. Never treat "the file is fresh" as guaranteed; surface `last-checked` in the page footer. ### 9.3 The override sheet (his editing surface) `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d//gviz/tq?tqx=out:csv&sheet=Publications` — verified working against a public sheet, returns plain CSV, **no API key or OAuth**. (Alternative: `.../pub?gid=0&single=true&output=csv` for File → Publish to web.) **Sheet 1 — `Publications`** (overrides, keyed on DOI): | doi | featured | student_authors | venue_override | title_override | pdf_url | exclude | notes | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 10.1038/s44304-026-00234-3 | TRUE | Padmini Ponukumati | | | | | cover paper | | 10.1016/j.ejrh.2025.103053 | | Sai Kiran Guniganti | | | | | | **Sheet 2 — `Manual`** (the four sections no API has — A Products, D Conference Presentations, E Invited Seminars, F Scientific Activities): | section | year | citation_text | url | |---|---|---|---| | Products | 2024 | SnapFlood — urban flood reporting platform | https://… | | Invited Seminars | 2025 | "Urban flooding in Indian cities", IISc Bangalore | | **Sheet 3 — `Students`** (alias map, because OpenAlex fragments coauthors): | student | aliases | |---|---| | Padmini Ponukumati | Padmini Ponukumati; P. Ponukumati | | BVNP Kambhammettu | B. V. N. P. Kambhammettu; BVN P Kambhammettu | ### 9.4 The build script (written and run — 55 → 38, byte-identical across runs) ```js const ORCID = '0000-0003-3188-9415' const TYPE_OK = new Set(['article', 'book-chapter', 'conference-paper']) const norm = t => (t || '').toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, ' ').trim() // 1. fetch by ORCID (not author.id — that ID can merge/split) const url = `https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=author.orcid:https://orcid.org/${ORCID}` + `&per-page=200&select=${SELECT}&sort=publication_date:desc` // 2. type filter let works = results.filter(w => TYPE_OK.has(w.type)) // 3. dedupe: DOI authoritative, FULL title as fallback — never a prefix const seen = new Map() for (const w of works) { const key = w.doi ? w.doi.toLowerCase().replace('https://doi.org/', '') : 'title:' + norm(w.title) const prev = seen.get(key) if (!prev || (!prev.doi && w.doi) || (!!prev.doi === !!w.doi && w.cited_by_count > prev.cited_by_count)) seen.set(key, w) } const titlesWithDoi = new Set([...seen.values()].filter(w => w.doi).map(w => norm(w.title))) works = [...seen.values()].filter(w => w.doi || !titlesWithDoi.has(norm(w.title))) // 4. self flag on ORCID (100% reliable), student flag on the alias set authors: w.authorships.map(a => ({ name: a.author.display_name, is_self: a.author.orcid === `https://orcid.org/${ORCID}`, is_student: studentAliases.has(a.author.display_name) })) // 5. deterministic order: date desc, then id asc as tiebreak .sort((a, b) => (b.date || '').localeCompare(a.date || '') || a.id.localeCompare(b.id)) ``` Determinism verified: two consecutive runs produced byte-identical `publications.json`. Output record: ```json { "id": "10.1038/s44304-026-00234-3", "doi": "10.1038/s44304-026-00234-3", "title": "Web-messaging-based dissemination of urban rainfall and flood information: a Telegram bot framework", "authors": [ { "name": "Padmini Ponukumati", "is_self": false, "is_student": true }, { "name": "Satish Kumar Regonda", "is_self": true, "is_student": false } ], "venue": "npj Natural Hazards", "year": 2026, "date": "2026-07-02", "volume": null, "issue": null, "pages": null, "type": "article", "cited_by": 0, "oa": "gold", "pdf": null, "featured": true } ``` ### 9.5 Journal-name fixes to hardcode ```js const JOURNAL_FIX = { 'npj natural hazards.': 'npj Natural Hazards', 'Journal of Hydrology Regional Studies':'Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies', 'Nonlinear processes in geophysics': 'Nonlinear Processes in Geophysics' } ``` ### 9.6 Borrowed conventions from al-folio (verified in its real source) Featured flag and custom fields, straight from `_bibliography/papers.bib`: ```bibtex @article{PhysRev.47.777, abbr={PhysRev}, title={Can Quantum-Mechanical Description of Physical Reality Be Considered Complete?}, author={Einstein*†, A. and Podolsky*, B. and Rosen*, N.}, journal={Phys. Rev.}, volume={47}, issue={10}, pages={777--780}, year={1935}, doi={10.1103/PhysRev.47.777}, selected={true}, annotation={* Example use of superscripts
† Albert Einstein} } ``` Self-highlighting from `_layouts/bib.liquid` — note it **strips marker glyphs before matching**, which is exactly how asterisks and daggers coexist with name matching: ```liquid {%- assign author_last_name = author.last | regex_replace: '[*∗†‡§¶‖&^]', '' -%} {% if site.scholar.last_name contains author_last_name %} {% if site.scholar.first_name contains author.first %}{% assign author_is_self = true %}{% endif %} {% endif %} ``` And `_config.yml` stores name variants as arrays: ```yaml scholar: last_name: [Einstein] first_name: [Albert, A.] style: apa ``` --- ## 10. Scholar indexing + structured data ### 10.1 Highwire Press meta tags From Google Scholar's official inclusion guidelines: - Scholar supports Highwire (`citation_title`), BE Press (`bepress_citation_title`) and PRISM (`prism.title`); **it prefers Highwire**. - **Minimum three fields**: title, full name of at least the first author, year of publication. Pages missing any one are *"processed as if they had no meta tags at all."* - Dates: *"Provide full dates in the '2010/5/12' format if available; or a year alone otherwise."* - Authors: *"Put each author name in a separate tag and omit all affiliations, degrees, certifications."* - PDFs: *"specify the locations of all full text versions using citation_pdf_url or DC.identifier tags"* — an unlinked PDF is not indexed. *"Failure to link the alternate versions together could result in incorrect indexing."* Verified live on `https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05233`: ```html ``` (arXiv uses `citation_date`; `citation_publication_date` is the canonical Highwire name — both are accepted.) Emit per paper page: ```html ``` Only worth doing if papers get individual URLs. **Do not put `citation_*` tags on a page listing many papers** — Scholar expects one paper per page. ### 10.2 JSON-LD One `Person` node, reused by `@id` across the site: ```json { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "Person", "@id": "https://satishregonda.in/#satish", "name": "Satish Kumar Regonda", "jobTitle": "Associate Professor", "affiliation": { "@type": "Organization", "name": "Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad", "url": "https://www.iith.ac.in/" }, "url": "https://satishregonda.in", "sameAs": ["https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3188-9415", "https://openalex.org/A5015401267", "https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=…"] } ``` Per paper (`ScholarlyArticle` inherits these from Article/CreativeWork/Thing): ```json { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "ScholarlyArticle", "headline": "Web-messaging-based dissemination of urban rainfall and flood information", "author": [{ "@id": "https://satishregonda.in/#satish" }], "datePublished": "2026-07-02", "isPartOf": { "@type": "PublicationIssue", "issueNumber": "1", "isPartOf": { "@type": "Periodical", "name": "npj Natural Hazards", "issn": "2948-2100" } }, "pageStart": "12", "identifier": { "@type": "PropertyValue", "propertyID": "DOI", "value": "10.1038/s44304-026-00234-3" }, "sameAs": "https://doi.org/10.1038/s44304-026-00234-3" } ``` Note `volumeNumber`/`issueNumber` are not direct `ScholarlyArticle` properties — nest them via `isPartOf` → `PublicationIssue` → `PublicationVolume` → `Periodical`. Also add an `Organization` node for the RAFT group with `parentOrganization` → IIT Hyderabad and `url` → raftwaters.in. --- ## 11. Ground truth: what his current page actually contains `https://sites.google.com/iith.ac.in/satishregonda/products-publications` (HTTP 200) is organised as: - **A. Products** — web-based tools ← no API has these - **B. In Referred Journals** ← OpenAlex covers this - **C. Book Chapters** ← OpenAlex covers this - **D. Presentations at Conferences** ← no API (the AGU abstracts in OpenAlex are noise, not this list) - **E. Invited Seminars** ← no API - **F. Scientific activities** ← no API His current citation format puts the year last: > "Saipriya, S.R., S. K. Regonda, and B. Rajagopalan, Space-time variability of rainfall attributes… https://doi.org/10.1016/j.uclim.2026.102950, 2026" Journal names are italicised, DOIs are hyperlinked, conference entries carry no DOI, and **no student co-authors are currently marked**. The asterisk convention is a new feature, not a migration of something existing — worth confirming with him that he wants it. **Design consequence:** the publications page needs a section model, not a flat auto-generated list. Only B and C are automated; A, D, E and F come from the `Manual` sheet.

exemplars.name: al-folio (Maruan Al-Shedivat, CMU) — the reference academic Jekyll theme
exemplars.what_works: Publications grouped by year in reverse-chronological order with year headers as dividers, generated entirely from a single papers.bib via jekyll-scholar. Each entry has a title, author list, venue, a collapsible abstract, a collapsible BibTeX block, and a row of small action buttons (DOI / HTML / PDF / Video / Code). Citation badges pull live counts from Google Scholar and Altmetric. A venue abbreviation badge (abbr) sits in a left gutter, giving the list a strong scannable vertical rhythm without clutter.
exemplars.steal_this: The three custom BibTeX fields that solve exactly our curation problems: selected={true} as the featured flag, abbr={} for the venue badge, and annotation={} for the asterisk legend. Plus the self-highlight regex from _layouts/bib.liquid, which strips [*∗†‡§¶‖&^] from the surname BEFORE matching — so student asterisks can live inside the BibTeX author field (author={Einstein*†, A. and ...}) and still match the name-highlight rule. Config stores name variants as arrays (last_name: [Regonda], first_name: [Satish, S., Satish Kumar]).

exemplars.name: arXiv (Cornell) — article abstract page
exemplars.what_works: A textbook-correct implementation of Highwire Press metadata: one <meta name="citation_author"> per author in 'Family, Given' order, citation_date in Google's 2024/11/07 format, citation_doi pointing at the published version rather than the preprint, and citation_pdf_url linking the full text so Scholar indexes the PDF against the abstract page rather than as an orphan.
exemplars.steal_this: The exact tag set and ordering to emit on each per-paper page, verbatim. Critically: one separate citation_author tag per author (never a comma-joined string), and always pair a hosted PDF with citation_pdf_url or Scholar will not index it at all.

exemplars.name: Efi Foufoula-Georgiou, UC Irvine — hydrology/geomorphology faculty site
exemplars.what_works: Separates the exhaustive record from the editorial one: distinct 'Publications', 'Research Highlights', 'Presentations' and 'Best Results' pages. That split serves two genuinely different visitors — a peer verifying the full record, and a prospective student or journalist wanting the three papers that matter. Links out to Google Scholar rather than duplicating metrics on-site.
exemplars.steal_this: The two-tier model, which maps directly onto our featured flag: a short curated 'Selected work' block on the homepage or top of the publications page, and the complete auto-generated list below it. Also the discipline of linking to Scholar for citation metrics instead of printing numbers that will drift out of date and contradict Scholar.

exemplars.name: Dr. Satish Regonda — current Google Sites page (the thing we are replacing)
exemplars.what_works: Its section model is the real requirement document: A. Products, B. In Referred Journals, C. Book Chapters, D. Presentations at Conferences, E. Invited Seminars, F. Scientific activities. Journal entries carry hyperlinked DOIs and italicised journal names; conference entries deliberately carry no DOI. He clearly thinks of software products and invited talks as first-class outputs alongside papers.
exemplars.steal_this: Preserve all six sections — no API covers A, D, E or F, so the new site needs a manual content lane regardless of how good the automation is. Also note what is absent: no student co-authors are currently marked anywhere, so the asterisk convention is a new feature to confirm with him rather than a migration.

exemplars.name: Google Scholar — official inclusion guidelines (Google)
exemplars.what_works: States the indexing contract precisely: Highwire tags are preferred over BE Press and PRISM; a minimum of three fields (title, first author's full name, year) is mandatory and pages missing any one are 'processed as if they had no meta tags at all'; dates use the 2010/5/12 format; each author needs its own tag with affiliations and degrees omitted.
exemplars.steal_this: The minimum-three-fields rule as a build-time assertion — fail the build if any paper page would emit fewer than citation_title + one citation_author + a year, rather than shipping pages Scholar silently ignores. Also the companion robots.txt fact: Allow /citations?user= but Disallow /citations?*cstart=, which is what makes automated full-profile scraping non-compliant.

pitfalls: DO NOT make ORCID or Crossref-by-ORCID the source of truth. Measured on his real record: ORCID has 14 works, Crossref's orcid filter has 5, OpenAlex has 55. Choosing either would silently publish a quarter of his career.

DO NOT dedupe on a truncated title prefix. It merges his two-part HEFS papers (10.1016/j.jhydrol.2014.05.028 'Part 1. Experimental design' and .030 'Part 2. Streamflow verification', 52 and 51 citations) into one entry and deletes a real publication. DOI first, full normalized title only as fallback.

DO NOT publish OpenAlex output unfiltered. His 55 records include 9 AGU/EGU conference abstracts, his own PhD thesis, a student's thesis, 5 preprints, and one record whose title is a reference-list parsing artifact: '2004), Temporal scaling in river flow: Can it be chaotic'. That on a faculty homepage looks careless.

DO NOT key the student-asterisk rule on author names or on OpenAlex author IDs. Neither is stable for his coauthors: Balaji Rajagopalan has 3 OpenAlex IDs, Kambhammettu appears as both 'B. V. N. P. Kambhammettu' (A5027162932) and 'BVN P Kambhammettu' (A5110805369), Azharuddin has 2 IDs, and one authorship has a null author id entirely. Only a manually maintained alias set works. (His OWN name is safe to match — the ORCID link keeps it to one ID and one spelling across all 55 works.)

DO NOT split OpenAlex author display_name into given/family naively. 17 of 77 coauthor names start with initials and many Indian names carry no reliable order marker — 'S.R. Saipriya' has no comma and no way to infer which part is the surname. Prefer rendering the name as-is over confidently reformatting it wrongly.

DO NOT print a bare citation count. OpenAlex says 524 for 10.1175/jcli-3272.1, Semantic Scholar 514, Crossref 380 — a 38% spread, and Google Scholar reports a fourth, higher number. Whatever you display will contradict the figure he quotes from Scholar. Either omit counts or stamp them 'Cited by 524 (OpenAlex, Sep 2026)'.

DO NOT re-host 'bronze' OA PDFs. Four of his 18 OA works have oa_status 'bronze' with license null — free to read on the publisher's site, no licence granted to anyone else. Only the 9 cc-by works are safe to mirror. Link the rest.

DO NOT assume the GitHub Action keeps running. Public-repo scheduled workflows are auto-disabled after 60 days of repository inactivity, and cron runs are routinely delayed 15+ minutes or skipped with no error and no notification. A refresh job that only commits when publications change will go quiet during a slow patch and then be silently switched off — the exact failure this whole system exists to prevent.

DO NOT let the scheduled job push to main. If it commits directly, an upstream metadata correction at OpenAlex rewrites his publication list without warning. Open a pull request instead so nothing reaches the live site unreviewed.

DO NOT rely on stale OpenAlex documentation. API keys became expected in February 2026 and pricing moved to credits/USD. The help docs also state a per-page maximum of 100, which is wrong — 200 works, 201 returns 'Pagination error.' Trust the live x-ratelimit-* response headers over any guide.

DO NOT scrape Google Scholar from CI. Its robots.txt allows /citations?user= but explicitly disallows /citations?*cstart=, the pagination parameter required to read a full profile. The `scholarly` package needs rotating proxies and CAPTCHA handling to work at all, and will get the runner's IP banned.

DO NOT call config.templates.add() on citation-js 0.8.2 — it throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined'. The method is plugins.config.get('@csl').styles.add(name, cslText). Also remember only apa, vancouver and harvard1 ship built in; every other CSL style must be registered from its .csl file. And water-resources-research.csl does not exist in the CSL repo (404) — use american-geophysical-union.csl.
DO NOT ship bibtexparser 2.x. The stable release is still 1.4.4; v2 has been sitting at 2.0.0b10 beta. Pin 1.4.x if you use the Python path at all.

DO NOT pipe raw ORCID JSON into the site. Its bulk works endpoint returns a contributors block containing coauthors' cleartext email addresses — I saw a real one in his record. Whitelist fields explicitly rather than passing the object through.

DO NOT check Semantic Scholar's openAccessPdf for null. It returns {"url": "", "status": null, "license": null} — an empty string, so a truthiness check on .url is required. Also don't promise tldr summaries: the field is rejected outright on /author/{id}/papers (400 error) and was null for his 2021 Water paper on the /paper endpoint.

DO NOT compare DOIs case-sensitively across sources. OpenAlex lowercases every DOI, Semantic Scholar uppercases them ('10.3390/W13091224'). Resolution itself is case-insensitive, so links work either way — but a case-sensitive dedup key silently creates duplicate entries.

DO NOT design the publications page as a single auto-generated list. His current page has six sections and the APIs cover only two of them (journals and book chapters). Products, conference presentations, invited seminars and scientific activities have no machine source at all and need a manual lane.

DO NOT emit citation_* meta tags on a page that lists many papers. Google Scholar expects one paper per page; putting them on the index page produces incorrect indexing. Only add them if papers get individual URLs.

DO NOT use example.com or a placeholder in Unpaywall's required email parameter — it returns HTTP 422 'Please use your own email address in API calls.' In practice you don't need Unpaywall at all, since OpenAlex already ingests it and exposes the same data via best_oa_location.
WATCH the pages field when mapping biblio: first_page and last_page are frequently identical in OpenAlex, which produces a redundant '102950-102950' range if joined blindly. Collapse when they match.
